description: A single-panel processing schematic — a temperature (T, vertical axis, origin marked "0") versus unlabeled time (horizontal axis) schedule for the hot rolling and annealing treatment of a steel. The path rises steeply to a plateau annotated "1200°C,1h", then a zigzag segment labelled "hot-rolling" descends through the rolling passes. Two horizontal dashed guide lines are drawn: an upper one labelled "880°C" (the finishing rolling temperature) and a lower one labelled "300°C". After rolling the curve is labelled "water cooled" and drops to the 300°C level, then continues with a shallower slope labelled "air cooled". On the right, a stack of six parallel horizontal lines is labelled "700°C~1200°C,1h", representing annealing at a set of temperatures from 700 to 1200 °C each held for 1 h; the uppermost and two lower lines are solid while intermediate ones are dashed. The final segment descends steeply and is labelled "water quenching". No time scale or numeric time values are printed. The figure visually defines the thermomechanical route that the citing text describes: forge at 1200 °C, hot-roll to a finishing temperature near 880 °C, quench to ~300 °C, then anneal at 700–1200 °C for 1 h and water quench.

observations.observation: The figure is a temperature-versus-time processing schematic with T on the vertical axis (origin labelled '0') and an unlabeled horizontal (time) axis; no time scale or numeric time ticks are printed.
The thermal path rises to a holding plateau labelled '1200°C,1h'.
A zigzag segment labelled 'hot-rolling' follows the 1200 °C plateau and crosses a dashed horizontal line labelled '880°C'.
A second dashed horizontal line is labelled '300°C' and the post-rolling segment labelled 'water cooled' descends to it, followed by a shallower 'air cooled' segment.
A stack of horizontal lines on the right is labelled '700°C~1200°C,1h', indicating annealing at a range of temperatures each held 1 h; upper and two lower lines are solid, intermediate lines dashed.
The final segment of the schedule descends steeply and is labelled 'water quenching'.
The caption states that Fig. 1 shows the hot rolling and annealing conditions of the steel.
The citing text states a 20 kg ingot of Fe–10Mn–10Al–0.7C steel was prepared by vacuum induction melting, heated to 1200 °C and forged to a 40 mm × 60 mm blank.
The citing text states the blank was homogenized at 1200 °C for 1 h, hot-rolled to 3 mm plate with finishing rolling temperature around 880 °C, then water quenched to about 300 °C.
The citing text states the hot-rolled plate was annealed at temperatures from 700 °C to 1200 °C for 1 h followed by water quenching.

The citing text refers to Fig. 1 as containing a Thermo-Calc calculated volume-fraction-versus-temperature plot of the phases; the supplied image shows only the temperature–time processing schedule, not such a plot.

subfigures.description: Temperature–time schematic of the hot rolling and annealing schedule; T on the vertical axis (origin '0'), time axis unlabeled. Path: heat to '1200°C,1h' plateau, zigzag 'hot-rolling' segment crossing the '880°C' dashed finishing-rolling line, 'water cooled' descent to the '300°C' dashed line, 'air cooled', then a stack of horizontal lines labelled '700°C~1200°C,1h' (annealing temperatures), ending in a descending arrow labelled 'water quenching'.
